fichas.title: Airport Networks and Aviation Market
fichas.summary: The page describes passenger and air-freight market segments, the hub-and-spoke model, low-cost airport operations, and airports’ growing reliance on commercial and office-space rental income. Airports also function as part of an inter-modal transport network.
figure_refs: Fig. 1, Aviation as part of the inter-modal transport network

fichas.title: Airport Planning and Regulatory Framework
fichas.summary: Airport construction and operation are guided by ICAO Convention Annex 14, Volume 1, national public planning law, airport regulations, and aviation-noise law. Large projects with regional significance may require a regional planning procedure and environmental assessment. The page notes that the ICAO has over 180 member countries.

fichas.title: Airport Environmental Planning and Operations
fichas.summary: Airport planning considers environmental protection, transport connections, and noise thresholds. The area on the ground affected by aircraft noise is described as a noise carpet. Operational measures include night-flying restrictions, noise-related fees, sound insulation, rainwater retention, careful use of de-icing chemicals, and energy, environmental, and waste management.

fichas.title: Hub Flight Nodes and Passenger Arrival Timing
fichas.summary: The diagrams illustrate flights grouped into time-of-day nodes at a major hub and passenger arrival patterns before scheduled departure. The arrival-time chart uses a horizontal scale labeled in minutes before departure, ending at planned take-off time; it is a scheduling diagram, not a building dimension.
